newsitem.title: USA: Electronic publisher Individual to buy ClariNet.
newsitem.headline: Electronic publisher Individual to buy ClariNet.

text.p: Electronic publisher Individual Inc. on Monday said it agreed to a definitive deal to acquire ClariNet Communications Corp. for about 1.5 million Individual shares, or $7.7 million.
Individual said privately held ClariNet, an Interent news company, has annual revenue of about $3.9 million and has shown a positive cash flow in each of the last five years.

"We believe this will keep us in line for turning profitable by the second half of 1998," said Bob Lentz, Individual's chief financial officer. In the meantime, he said, his company planned to make additional, unspecified investments in ClariNet.
The transaction is expected to be effective within the next week.
Individual's stock was unchanged at $5.125 on Nasdaq.
ClariNet was employee-owned and funded predominantly from internal cash flow. It had 1.5 million licensed readers as of early 1997.
ClariNet's services are provided to more than 350 Internet Service Providers, corporations and educational institutions, who in turn incorpate ClariNet in their own services.
Brad Templeton, ClariNet's founder, and Roy Folk, its president and chief operating officer, will become officers of Individual in addition to their operating roles at ClariNet.
Templeton also will be one of Individual's largest shareholders, with about 7 percent of the outstanding shares. All 40 of ClariNet's staff will become Individual employees.
ClariNet will continue to operate from its headquarters in San Jose, Calif.
Individual is based in Burlington, Mass.
The acquisition of ClariNet is the second by Individual in as many weeks. On June 6, Individual acquired CompanyLink, a research product from Delphi Internet Services.

Individual said it will explore ways to add advertising to ClariNet's products. Advertising revenue now accounts for less than 5 percent of ClariNet's revenue, which is dominated by subscription fees.

"Plans for adding advertising to some of our products are in process already," said ClariNet's Templeton. "Individual's very capable advertising sales organisation can help us accelerate that effort."
